messages:
maya: Heads-up — heatmap charts in EU are janking hard since ~11:05. p95 render jumped from ~120ms to ~420ms, users seeing frameskips. Anyone else?

raj: Yep, I noticed slow paints on /dashboards/usage-heatmap. Started right after the routing-policy rollout.

sam: deploy-bot: canary deploy quota-routing-v2 -> 10% at 2026-03-20T11:03:12Z (sha: a1b2c3d).

maya: Correlating telemetry now — kv_cache_hit_rate for heatmaps dropped: 0.88 -> 0.57 around 11:05. Also chart_prefetch_v2 feature flag flipped in the same window.

olivia: Build diff shows charting-lib +82KB (tree-shake change). Not huge but could push more parsing on main thread if combined with cache misses.

raj: Can someone dump a trace? I can check client-side CPU and main-thread busy: do we have a flame on long tasks for paint/layout?

maya: Pasted a small perf snippet: ```Long Task at 11:05:43 main-thread 180ms (parse+compile charting.js:line 420) FrameDrop spike traceId=trace-9987```

sam: Two hypotheses: (1) routing change shifted more traffic to EU edge causing kv cache affinity misses, (2) prefetch change changed request ordering so more chunks load synchronously.

olivia: Also see bundle lazy-load priority changed in the last feature PR (PR #4321). It inlines a small chunk for heatmap interactions — maybe it's now blocking render while cache warms.

raj: Quick repro: open the heatmap, filter -> heavy query, toggle time range. I can repro locally with canary flag on.

maya: For mitigation — can we flip chart_prefetch_v2 off and/or revert routing canary? Which is faster to rollback?

sam: Easiest is to flip the FF: ```curl -X POST https://flags.internal/ff -d '{"flag":"chart_prefetch_v2","value":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'``` that should be immediate. Reverting the routing policy requires infra approval and might take longer.

deploy-bot: initiate-flag-change chart_prefetch_v2=false by sam at 2026-03-20T11:18:05Z

maya: Doing the flag toggle now. Will wait ~2 mins and recheck metrics.

raj: Meanwhile I'm collecting kv-cache debug stats and affinity mapping across our EU nodes. If the routing change spread traffic across nodes without priming cache, that explains the hit_rate collapse.

olivia: If flag flip helps, we still need a follow-up: isolate whether bundle parse or kvcache miss is dominant. Could be combined effect (more parse work per request + more cache misses = amplification).

maya: Flag flip complete — dashboard samples: p95 render dropped back to ~150ms, kv_cache_hit_rate climbing back to 0.79. Early sign that prefetch change was the main amplifier. :relieved:

raj: Nice. I'll keep digging into the affinity issue — collecting node histograms now. If we see sustained cross-node churn we should roll routing back.

sam: Filing a quick perf regression ticket: PROD-6623 with reproducer, traces, and logs. Assigning to @raj (investigate affinity) and @maya (verify UX rollouts).

olivia: Also opening PR to revert the inlining change in charting-lib for a non-blocking chunk—will link in the ticket (PR #4337).

maya: Thanks all. Follow-ups:
- raj: deep-dive on kvcache affinity + routing policy metrics (node histograms, per-node heatmap misses)
- olivia: revert/soft-fix chart chunking and add deferral for heavy parse work
- sam: add canary gating to chart_prefetch_v2 (ramped slower, telemetry guard)

sam: Quick note — add a canary metric: console.chart_render.p75 and kvcache.hit_rate to the rollout guard so future flips auto-pause if either regresses >20%.

deploy-bot: ticket PROD-6623 created by sam.

maya: I'll follow up with a short postmortem once we have the affinity graphs. Thanks for the fast triage. :thumbsup:
